title: The Pulse, Thursday 9 October 2026
tldr: OpenAI withdrew three math papers after community pushback, while Anthropic cut Sonnet 5.5 cache reads in half and announced API credits for Max/Team plans. Claude Code is being used to discover planets, and a 16.9 MB speech model just showed up on Hacker News.

models.title: StepFun Step 5 Preview
models.summary: A 27B active / 600B sparse MoE with 1M context, optimized for agentic work and software engineering, now on OpenRouter.
models.why: Large context and agentic focus fits our Hermes workflows; if it runs well on agent tasks it's worth testing against Sonnet and Sol for code and analysis work.

models.title: OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast
models.summary: Near-Astra intelligence at up to 8x faster speeds than Sol Standard, rolling out to the API, Codex, and ChatGPT Work.
models.why: 8x faster Sol means our Codex and Claude Code jobs finish sooner, cutting latency on reviews, code generation, and agent work.

research.title: From Retrieval to Reconstruction: Constructing Evolvable Cognitive Memory for Long-Term Dialogue
research.summary: A memory system that distinguishes source-attributed beliefs from unattributed facts, enabling long-term dialogue agents to reason reliably over extended interactions.
research.why: EverRaise voice agents and our own Mnemosyne work could benefit from separating what the agent learned from what the user stated, especially for multi-session calls.

research.title: DuplexAgent-RSI: Recursive Harness Improvement for Full-Duplex Voice Agent Collaboration
research.summary: A full-duplex model stays on the live channel while complex reasoning and tool use are delegated asynchronously, solving the latency-vs-capability trade-off in voice agents.
research.why: EverRaise runs Vapi voice agents, and this pattern—lightweight duplex front-end plus async delegation—maps directly to what we build for call grading and lead nurturing.

research.title: All Verdicts are Not Equal: Rethinking LLM Judge Reliability
research.summary: A comprehensive reliability audit of LLM-as-a-Judge across six models, four benchmarks, and varying prompts, showing systemic variance often treated as ground truth.
research.why: We use LLM judges in the wehshi review panel and for evaluating prompt outputs; understanding their brittleness helps us calibrate confidence in automated verdicts.

research.title: SWE-Journey: Towards More Realistic Evaluation of Coding Assistants through Long-Horizon, Multi-Turn Interaction
research.summary: A benchmark for coding assistants that spans long chains of development work in evolving repositories, with repeated requirement clarification—closer to real-world Codex and Claude Code use.
research.why: Our team uses Claude Code and Codex daily; a benchmark that mirrors actual multi-turn, evolving-repo workflows is a better calibration tool than one-shot tasks.

releases.title: LangChain 1.4.4
releases.summary: Fixes retry logic for summarization middleware on context overflow, plus dependency bumps.
releases.why: We use LangChain for retrieval and agent flows in Pipeline's clients; retry on overflow is a common edge case in longer documents.

releases.title: LangChain Core 1.6.9
releases.summary: Adds support for passing a callable to with_retry.
releases.why: Custom retry logic is useful for rate-limited APIs; if we're hitting OpenRouter or vendor endpoints with dynamic backoff, this gives us the hook.

releases.title: Langfuse 4.55.0
releases.summary: Adds support for OpenAI decision models in evals, FIPS-mode base images, skill imports from ZIPs, and batch score processing.
releases.why: We trace with Langfuse; batch score processing and decision model support fit our review and agent eval workflows.

hackernews.title: OpenAI Withdraws 3 Math Papers
hackernews.summary: OpenAI retracted three mathematical results from its public repo after community scrutiny.
hackernews.why: When we rely on vendor benchmarks or published research for model selection, this is a reminder to verify claims ourselves before betting production work on them.

hackernews.title: Whistle: Speech to Text in 16.9 MB
hackernews.summary: A 16.9 MB speech-to-text model, tiny enough to run anywhere, with competitive accuracy.
hackernews.why: EverRaise voice agents process transcripts in real time; a model this small could run on-device or in edge functions with near-zero latency.

hackernews.title: I think I found a planet nobody knew existed. I used Claude Code to find it
hackernews.summary: A user claims Claude Code helped discover a previously unknown planet through data analysis.
hackernews.why: This is one data point on how far coding agents have come—enabling domain work (astronomy data crunching) for non-domain experts.

hackernews.title: OpenAI annualised revenues $20B less than previously signalled
hackernews.summary: OpenAI's annualized revenue is $20 billion below earlier projections.
hackernews.why: No direct use for us yet—but it's the talk of the day and signals the AI market's volatility matters for pricing and vendor stability.

x_posts.title: Anthropic adds monthly API credits to Max and Team plans
x_posts.summary: $100 on Max 5x, $200 on Max 20x, and up to $500 pooled on Team, usable on any Claude model.
x_posts.why: Our team runs on Claude subscriptions; API credits let us script more work without separate billing, useful for cron jobs and Hermes automations.

x_posts.title: Anthropic cuts Sonnet 5.5 cache reads in half
x_posts.summary: Cache reads now $0.10 per million tokens (was $0.20), making Sonnet 5.5 ~20% cheaper on agentic work.
x_posts.why: We use Sonnet 5.5 for agent work and PR reviews; 20% cheaper cache reads means our wehshi panel runs cost less per review.

x_posts.title: Hermes Agent now in the Microsoft Store
x_posts.summary: One-click install for Hermes Agent on Windows, with more updates for the Windows ecosystem coming.
x_posts.why: We run Hermes Agent as Botterfly; easier distribution helps onboard clients and partners who want to try the agent on their own machines.

x_posts.title: Building effective agent automations with Claude Managed Agents
x_posts.summary: A guide to deploying agents that read Slack/GitHub on a schedule with credentials and memory, using Claude Code and the new API credits.
x_posts.why: This is the same pattern we use for The Pulse and other cron jobs; the official guide might have shortcuts we missed.

closing: Releases: Next.js shipped only canaries in the window, so the three LangChain and Langfuse releases above are the notable ones.
